Definition: of uncertain derivation; blood, literally (of men or animals), figuratively (the juice of grapes) or specially (the atoning blood of Christ); by implication, bloodshed, also kindred:--blood.
BiblicalUsage: haîma means blood. In Matthew 16:17, the text says "for flesh and blood hath not revealed [it] unto thee." In Mark 5:25, the text says "which had an issue of blood twelve years."
TheologicalSignificance: What haîma teaches me is that salvation is God's work from first to last — we receive it, we do not achieve it. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Jairus' Daughter and the Bleeding Woman; Peter's Confession at Caesarea Philippi
